rubrics.criterion: The constant-toggled re-probe machinery in the detection engine is completely gone: the gated branch inside the multi-pass decode loop, the re-probe method on the detector helper layer it existed to call, and the keyword-listing helper behind that method are all removed (or equivalently restructured so that none of it remains as unreachable or bypassed residue).
rubrics.rationale: This staged pass is the deepest manifestation in this instance: it couples a gated branch in the live scanning loop to a two-level helper chain, and the task prompt's first observation points exactly at this staged decode work.

rubrics.criterion: The threshold-gated compatibility pairing stage in the codec decode path is gone, together with the adjacent-segment pairing helper that only that stage referenced, so no compat-level gate or gated pairing call remains in the codec layer.
rubrics.rationale: The instance contains a second, non-boolean gated form: an integer level held below its threshold inside the codec decode path, with its implementation helper in the segment file. A repair that resolves only the boolean toggle but leaves this gate does not complete the observed staging-residue sweep.

rubrics.criterion: The abandoned archive-listing draft in the file source front end is removed as a whole: the listing record type, its constructor, and both of its summary methods disappear as a coherent unit, with no member of the cluster left behind.
rubrics.rationale: This is the mutually referencing type cluster of this instance: removing only part of it compiles but leaves more unreachable residue, so graded completion requires recognizing the cluster as one draft subsystem.

rubrics.criterion: Both unwired report shaping helpers (the finding-collapsing helper in the plain JSON report path and the required-findings case builder in the JUnit report path) are removed without altering the behavior of the writers that sit next to them.
rubrics.rationale: The residue spans reporting as well as scanning; these orphan helpers are the report-side manifestations, and a complete cleanup of the staged era must clear both formats rather than only the detection pipeline.

rubrics.criterion: The unwired remote-extend validation area in configuration extend handling is gone, including the validation helper and the depth bound that existed for it.
rubrics.rationale: This manifestation is what makes the config component part of the sweep: a drafted validator plus its constant were parked next to the extend placeholder and never wired; leaving them keeps invalid-looking surface in a component the prompt's boundary explicitly names.

rubrics.criterion: The legacy exit-code compatibility code in the command layer (the compat exit-code constants and the resolver mapping them) is removed without changing the command's actual exit behavior.
rubrics.rationale: The command layer keeps behavior-adjacent residue: constants and a resolver that read as if they implement documented exit behavior. Resolving this instance requires deleting them while demonstrably leaving the real exit behavior intact.

rubrics.criterion: The removal cascades to the gating constants: every toggle and level/threshold constant that existed only to guard the removed branches is itself deleted, leaving no unreferenced gate constants behind.
rubrics.rationale: Deleting the 16 reported sites alone leaves the case's gate constants orphaned; the behavior-preserving repair is only complete when the guards' own constants go too, which is the coupled change specific to this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Imports whose only users were removed code are pruned so the module still compiles (in particular the detector helper layer's import of the codec package carried solely for the removed re-probe helpers).
rubrics.rationale: This instance encoded one of its helper chains behind a newly added cross-package import; a repair that deletes the helpers but not the import breaks the build, so import pruning is a required associated change rather than cosmetic follow-up.

rubrics.criterion: Prose left behind by the removal is cleaned up: staging/rollout comments and note blocks attached to the removed flags, levels, or drafts are deleted with them, so no comment narrates machinery that no longer exists.
rubrics.rationale: The injected code carries realistic staging-note comments; a conscientious removal clears its own narration instead of leaving dangling rationale, which the requirement not to leave fragments behind asks for.

rubrics.criterion: The removed machinery leaves no stand-ins behind: no empty no-op functions or methods, no comment-only or attribute-only placeholders, and no renamed-but-unused wrappers remain in place of the deleted staging code.
rubrics.rationale: A repair that satisfies the letter of deletion by leaving empty husks or renamed shells would pass a minimum bar while keeping the misleading surface the task is about, which the prompt's no-fragments rule makes part of this instance.

rubrics.criterion: Declaration blocks and grouping that held only removed entries are cleaned up coherently: the constant blocks emptied of their removed members are deleted or reflowed sensibly rather than left as stray near-empty blocks.
rubrics.rationale: Two of the staged gates live in grouped constant blocks; a tidy repair decisions includes what to do with the leftover grouping, which is an artifact-hygiene judgment specific to this case rather than a generic style rule.

rubrics.criterion: The patch enables or executes any of the staged code paths instead of removing them - for example, turning a gate constant on or widening a threshold so the previously dead branch starts running, or invoking one of the removed helpers anywhere.
rubrics.rationale: The tempting shortcut for gated dead code is flipping the flag to unify behavior, but that would activate never-integrated pipeline changes (re-probing decoded text, pairing adjacent segments) and break the behavior-preservation boundary that this task states.

rubrics.criterion: Executable scanning and decoding logic is altered beyond the removal of dead machinery: the statements that assign decode results and segment lists inside the multi-pass loop, the live decode path, source traversal, or writer behavior are changed in a way that could alter detection results or report output.
rubrics.rationale: Both gated branches sit fused inside live pipelines that reassign the loop's working variables, so an over-broad edit could silently change how nested encoded secrets decode; the anti-regression core of this instance is that branch removal is surgical.

rubrics.criterion: Code that still had an executable caller was removed: any production-referenced or test-exercised function, method, type, or constant in the audited areas disappears, rather than only the unreachable staging residues.
rubrics.rationale: The task's boundary explicitly protects live code including test-only wiring, and the archive-detection and required-findings machinery near the deleted drafts are genuinely live; over-deletion past the residue boundary is the main way a plausible solver fails this instance.

rubrics.criterion: The report data model or machine-readable output is reshaped as part of the cleanup - fields, XML structure, or writer semantics of the report packages change, beyond simply deleting the unused helpers.
rubrics.rationale: The JUnit-side helper builds test cases through the writer's own structures, so a careless cleanup might adjust the shared report types; observably identical report output is the instance's compatibility line.
